# HEN COMMERCIAL ANALYTICS — MORNING BRIEF
## Tuesday, 2026-11-03 | ERCOT BESS Fleet (32 Nodes)

---

## 1. PERFORMANCE SUMMARY

Yesterday's fleet RT average of **$24.87/MWh** continued the three-day deceleration from the elevated **$74.66/MWh** spike environment on 10/31, confirming a structural shift toward oversupplied, renewable-heavy conditions. The negative price node count expanded sharply to **18 nodes** (vs. 14 on 11/01 and just 3 on 10/31), with West Texas locations — TOYAH_RN, SADLBACK_RN, FAULKNER_RN, COYOTSPR_RN, RTLSNAKE_BT, CEDRVALE_RN, and others — bearing the brunt of wind/solar overgeneration. The four spike nodes (**MAINLAND_RN, GRDNE_ESR_RN, CISC_RN, RUSSEKST_RN** reaching a fleet peak of **$986.43/MWh**) represent localized congestion-driven RT outperformance, not broad market tightness. Assets at those four nodes that dispatched in RT captured significant upside; the MCC data confirms CISC_RN (+$62.06/MWh) and MAINLAND_RN (+$60.84/MWh) received material congestion benefits via constraint 6635__G and MDOPHR99_A respectively. The dominant story fleet-wide is accelerating RT price suppression from renewable overcollection — operators at 18 nodes faced negative RT prices, making DA commitment the value-preserving strategy at most locations yesterday.

The +$23.97/MWh positive MCC (BLESSI_PAVLOV1_1 constraint, avg shadow $123.37/MWh, binding HE08) adds a structural congestion tailwind that reinforces DA commitment. Full DA energy offer is recommended; no RT reservation is warranted absent a significant forecast revision.

## 4. WEATHER & LOAD OUTLOOK

**Today (11/03):** A moisture-driven weather system is sweeping coastal and central Texas — Austin (100% precip), Houston IAH (89%), San Antonio (82%), Galveston (59%), Victoria (70%) — but West Texas (Midland 2%, Lubbock 5%) remains dry. Cloud cover along the coast will suppress solar generation today, potentially tightening afternoon prices in the Houston/South zones. Wind generation should remain strong in West Texas given dry, unseasonably mild conditions. Net effect: **modest upward RT price pressure in coastal/central load zones today, continued suppression in West Texas renewables zones.**

**Near-term (11/04–11/06):** The storm system exits quickly — precipitation drops to single digits across most of Texas by 11/04. Mild temperatures statewide (highs 63–85°F) with moderate lows will keep heating/cooling loads well below seasonal stress levels. Gross load is unlikely to materially exceed the 65.9 GW baseline; the renewable-heavy oversupply pattern that drove 18 negative-price nodes on 11/02 could persist or deepen. **Expect continued low fleet RT averages and elevated negative-price node count mid-week.**

**Extended (11/07–11/09):** A cool front appears in the 7-day forecast — Midland drops to a high of 59°F (11/07, 24% precip), Lubbock 61°F, DFW 66°F. This modest cooling, combined with elevated precip probabilities across South Texas (Brownsville 64–88% through the weekend), could increase load slightly while reducing solar output. However, temperatures remain far above heating demand thresholds. **No significant price spike catalyst identified in the 7-day window; West Texas renewable suppression is the dominant pricing dynamic.**

**Strategic implication:** The improving renewable output / mild load environment through mid-November favors DA premium capture at most nodes and aggressive charging during negative-price windows at West Texas nodes. Reserve RT discharge for the four spike-capable congestion nodes (MAINLAND_RN, CISC_RN, RUSSEKST_RN, GRDNE_ESR_RN).
